blog_numbers: Convergence, pass after one review-and-fix round: 65% before, 78% after the convergence work (adoption bar for F-convergence arms: a relative gain of that order, recall held)
Convergence, PRs needing five or more rounds: 8.9% before, 1.5% after (bar for round-cap / no-repeat / diff-only arms)
Convergence, mean reviews to pass: 2.08 before, 1.32 after (bar for convergence arms)
Revert share of merged PRs fell by more than 40% from June to September while merged PRs more than doubled (guardrail: an arm may not raise the escaped-bug rate)
Share of internal PRs with substantive review comments rose from 16% to 54% at research-preview launch (bar for finder arms on bug PRs; must not rise on clean PRs)
About 59% of what the reviewer kept flagging (git blame) was code present since its first pass (compare with late-round findings in replay loops, e.g. #38)
Most PRs over 1,000 lines get findings; most small ones come back clean (stratify results by size; #33 at +19/-14 is a counterexample)
One CLI PR ran more than fifty review-and-fix rounds overnight (runaway-loop check for the no-cap arm)
Round cap at three rounds, then step back and reconsider (trace's current value; the cap arm tests none/2/3/5)
Verification estimated to make the final result two to three times better (Boris Cherny; motivation for A-verify-before-review)
Risk tiers: Low needs no human approval once automated and security checks are green, Medium one person, High two people (approvals not testable; tier contents used for tier-table-vs-bug-sources)
Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code's own code (context only)
Anthropic monorepo changes landing per day: about 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September (context only)
A typical CLI PR may run dozens of checks before anyone looks (context only; this repo has one local `npm run check`)
Human-time metrics: human approvals per PR at median and 95th percentile, human comments, time a PR waits on a person (proxy only here)
